Country.evidence_source: The BAS-2 was translated into Polish by three professional translators. The translations were compared and discussed by the authors. The agreed version was then back-translated (Sousa & Rojjanasrirat, 2011) by two other psychologists who were fluent in English. The translations were reviewed by the authors and some minor modifications were implemented. To assess item and score equivalence of English and Polish versions of the BAS-2, a study was conducted in a bilingual group of English Studies Master's degree students (53 women, 17 men).

Sample.evidence_source: To assess item and score equivalence of English and Polish versions of the BAS-2, a study was conducted in a bilingual group of English Studies Master's degree students (53 women, 17 men). The sample for the equivalence assessment was 53 women + 17 men = 70 participants. The sizes of the 'first subsample' and 'second subsample' for the main data collection are not provided.
Sample.warning: The sample size of 70 refers only to the bilingual group used for BAS-2 equivalence assessment. The sizes of the other two subsamples for the main data collection are not specified.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the procedure for translating the BAS-2 into Polish and assessing its equivalence with the English version. A study was conducted with a bilingual group of 70 English Studies Master's degree students (53 women, 17 men) for this equivalence assessment. Subsequently, data were collected from two unspecified subsamples using anonymous paper-and-pencil questionnaires, recruited via personal contacts.
